cards.text: Paul, the apostle who wrote this letter, is wrapping it up for the Galatians. Now he picks up the pen and writes with his own hand. I don't know about you, friend, but when somebody writes it BY HAND, I'm reading every word.

cards.question: Paul tells the Galatians to look at how tiny his handwriting is.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then Paul calls out some people who want to make a good impression on the outside. They're trying to compel the Galatians to be circumcised. All sprinkles, no cookie.

cards.question: Paul says these people pushing circumcision have a reason. What is it?

answers.text: To avoid persecution for the cross of Christ
To bring the Galatians back to Jerusalem
To earn a place among the apostles

cards.question: Paul says the people pushing circumcision keep the law themselves.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: So what do these people want out of the Galatians getting circumcised?

answers.text: To boast in the Galatians' flesh
To report them to the priests
To make them leaders in Galatia

cards.text: Now Paul flips it: "But as for me…" Friend, if it were me, I'd boast about my brand new edges for a WEEK straight. Paul's got one thing on his list.

cards.question: Paul says he'll never boast, except in the ___ of our Lord Jesus Christ.

answers.text: cross
law
temple

cards.question: Through the cross of Christ, what does Paul say has happened between him and the world?

answers.text: The world has been crucified to him and he to the world
The world has made peace with him and he with the world
The world has forgotten him and he has forgotten the world

cards.text: Then Paul takes the whole circumcision question and settles it in one line. Mic drop. Well. PEN drop.

cards.question: Paul says being uncircumcised is what really counts.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Neither circumcision nor uncircumcision means anything, Paul says. What counts is a new ___.

answers.text: creation
tradition
promise

cards.text: Paul talks about the ones who walk by this rule. And he's got a blessing for every single one of them.

cards.question: What does Paul wish on all who walk by this rule?

answers.text: Peace and mercy
Wealth and long life
Strength and wisdom

cards.text: And Paul says that blessing goes "even to the Israel of God."
Then Paul draws a line: "From now on let no one cause me trouble." That's Paul putting his whole life on Do Not Disturb.

cards.question: Why does Paul say no one should cause him trouble from now on?

answers.text: He bears the marks of Jesus on his body
He is leaving Galatia to sail for Rome
He has finished his work as an apostle

cards.text: And Paul signs off with one last blessing for his brothers.

cards.question: In his final blessing, what does Paul pray will be with the Galatians' spirit?

answers.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ
The power of our Lord Jesus Christ
The wisdom of our Lord Jesus Christ

cards.text: Then he seals it with one word: "Amen." Now THAT'S how you close a letter, friend. Not "Sent from my phone."
